solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Five arriving at once with unknown illness

parts.note: quins are quintuplets, five babies born together
Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A woman has quintuplets and promptly falls ill with something nobody can name.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinsy is a specific throat illness, an abscess beside the tonsils, so it is an example of the wider category.

clue.text: Abruptly abandon shy Norway rat

indicators.note: cut off abruptly, so the word for abandon loses its final letter

parts.note: to abandon is to quit
to shy is to throw, to sling

explanation.surface: Someone flees in sudden panic from a timid brown rat of the species found in Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norway rat' looks like zoology (it is a real name for the brown rat) but means a Norwegian traitor: Vidkun Quisling collaborated with the Nazi occupiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat is slang for a traitor, and the eponym of Norway's wartime collaborator became the general word for one.

clue.text: Unfortunate old men lie drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: It is a sorry sight: elderly men lying around intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-omened is inauspicious, attended by bad luck, hence unfortunate.

clue.text: All there is can be invisible at first

indicators.note: each of the three words has its opening letter made invisible, so those letters are removed

explanation.surface: A philosophical musing that everything in existence might start out unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is all there is mentally sound, an idiom for being of sound mind.

clue.text: Hairy nuns have denied embracing

indicators.note: the words nuns have denied hold the answer within them, running across their breaks

explanation.surface: The nuns deny they have been hugging anyone hairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A face not shaved is stubbly or bearded, so hairy is a looser synonym.

clue.text: Amendment to feature Biden's 24, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner's name signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: Joe Biden's first name with the possessive gives the word joe's
the answer to 24 down is a slang word for the head; nob is another

explanation.surface: A wry suggestion that the US president's face could use some changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of JOE'S NOB gives NOSE JOB; the swap is by sound, since the written vowels differ.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose job is cosmetic surgery on the nose, a facial feature being altered, hence an amendment to it.

clue.text: Passed on woman's European journal about this, but not man's

parts.note: her is the possessive used for a woman

indicators.note: about means the journal goes around what follows

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

indicators.note: but not tells us to remove the man's word from this

parts.note: his is the possessive used for a man

explanation.surface: A woman's diary is handed down in the family, while the man's is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not man's' is not a contrast in the story: it tells you to strip the possessive pronoun from 'this', leaving a single letter for 'about' to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary trait or title is one passed on from parent to child.

clue.text: Old Sanskrit section of comparative dictionary

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A philologist consults the ancient Sanskrit entries in a comparative dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Vedic is the archaic form of Sanskrit in which the Vedas were composed.

clue.text: Tired arguments in outskirts of Derby

indicators.note: in puts the arguments within the letters taken from the city
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: rows are quarrels or arguments

explanation.surface: Residents on the edge of Derby, an English Midlands city, are worn out by their disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowsy means sleepy, a close synonym of tired.

clue.text: The French on holiday don't hold back!

parts.note: le is a French word for the
a trip is a holiday or outing

explanation.surface: A cheerful exhortation to French holidaymakers to let their hair down.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom for acting without restraint, the imperative of not holding back.

clue.text: Lesbians perhaps cooking large sardines

indicators.note: cooking suggests the ingredients are worked into a different form

explanation.surface: Some women preparing a big pan of sardines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lesbians' here means people from Lesbos, the Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of the island of Lesbos are by definition islanders, making them an example.

clue.text: Short farewell east of river channel

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means to the right of, so the river comes first
short means the farewell loses its last letter

parts.note: adios is a Spanish farewell

explanation.surface: A curt goodbye said somewhere on the eastern bank of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio is a broadcasting medium, and a channel is a medium of communication, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Feeble American wearing lingerie inside out

indicators.note: the outer letters wear, or surround, the American
with its inside taken out, only the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A weak American has put underwear on back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lame means weak or unconvincing, as in a lame excuse, a synonym for feeble.

clue.text: Harms judge during vigorous pedicures

indicators.note: during places the judge within the reworked letters
vigorous suggests the letters are energetically shaken up

explanation.surface: A judge suffers injury in the middle of an overly energetic foot treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To prejudice something is to damage or jeopardise it, as in prejudicing a case, so a verb synonym.

clue.text: Working class pined for tranquillity

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked over into a new shape

explanation.surface: The labouring classes long for some peace and quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Placidness is calmness, the quality of being serene, a synonym for tranquillity.

clue.text: Indefinite number working, knocking back beer and offering resistance

parts.note: N is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number
a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: knocking back is read as turning the beer around

parts.note: pils is a pilsner lager

explanation.surface: Someone working while downing countless beers still manages to resist.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonslip surface offers resistance to sliding, so it grips.

clue.text: Buttocks burgeon over time, ultimately vast

indicators.note: the burgeoning word goes over, or covers, the following letters

parts.note: to boom is to burgeon or grow rapidly

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of vast

explanation.surface: Someone's backside grows over the years until it is enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom is the everyday word for the seat of the body, a synonym of buttocks.

clue.text: Trim plain tripe in state of heightened activity

indicators.note: trim means each of the two words loses its final letter

parts.note: overt means plain, open to view
tripe is nonsense, drivel

explanation.surface: A butcher is told to tidy up some plain tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' acts on both words: OVERT loses its T and DRIVEL its L.
explanation.definitionFit: In overdrive describes working at full intensity, an idiom for heightened activity.

clue.text: I agree to stop 8 in faculty

indicators.note: to stop means the agreement plugs a gap inside the number

parts.note: 8 here is the number written in words, not a cross-reference
yes is how one says I agree

explanation.surface: A tired person agrees to stop at an university faculty.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' looks like a reference to 8 down; it is simply the number spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the power of seeing, one of the bodily faculties or senses.

clue.text: 7 losing case seconds after court orders

indicators.note: after puts the seconds behind the court
losing its case means the word sheds its outer letters

parts.note: the answer to 7 down, the old Sanskrit word

explanation.surface: A court issues rulings after an ancient text loses a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: Edicts are official decrees or proclamations, in other words orders.

clue.text: Hide damage from boy, reportedly smart

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for boy is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a son is a boy
to smart is to sting or burn

explanation.surface: A boy apparently feels the sting of a lie meant to conceal harm he did.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunburn is reddening and damage to the skin, and hide is a word for skin.

clue.text: Senior nurses strongly advise ending of unnecessary operations

indicators.note: nurses means holds, so senior wraps round the advice

parts.note: to urge is to strongly advise

indicators.note: ending of picks the last letter of unnecessary

explanation.surface: Senior nurses advise strongly against needless surgical procedures.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery is the general term for operations on the body, a collective synonym.

clue.text: Tough 24 hours without answers

indicators.note: without means the answers are taken out

parts.note: a day of 24 hours, here one day of the week, Saturday
A is the standard abbreviation for answer, so answers gives two of them

explanation.surface: A hard full day spent without any solutions.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' looks like a cross-reference to 24 down but is just part of '24 hours', a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy means robust and strongly built, a synonym for tough.

clue.text: Brahms and Liszt left in 16 briefly

indicators.note: in places the left inside the shortened word
briefly means cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the answer to 16 across, the word for buttocks

explanation.surface: Two composers are left sitting on their backsides.
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms and Liszt is Cockney rhyming slang for 'pissed', i.e. drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for very drunk, as is the rhyming slang of the composers' names.

clue.text: Lustful librarian promises to muffle noise

parts.note: Lib. is a dictionary abbreviation for librarian

indicators.note: to muffle means the promises wrap round the noise

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay
din is loud noise

explanation.surface: A randy librarian vows to keep the noise down.
explanation.definitionFit: Libidinous means having strong sexual desire, a formal synonym of lustful.

clue.text: Nut formerly supporting bishop

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means placed below, so the bishop goes on top

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
once means formerly, at one time

explanation.surface: A nut that used to prop up a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonce is British slang for the head, as is nut.

clue.text: Likelihood of dodos appearing regularly?

indicators.note: appearing regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A wry question about the chances of extinct dodos turning up again.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds measure probability, so they express a likelihood.

clue.text: Ignoring the 25, not really vocal

indicators.note: 25 across is the word for chance or probability; ignoring the odd-numbered letters keeps the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone who disregards the chances is not actually outspoken.
explanation.walkthrough: The 25 across answer is a word that also means odd-numbered: drop letters 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken aloud by voice, so it is a synonym of vocal.

clue.text: Touch can dissolve innards of Geraldine

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: dissolving its innards leaves only the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: A grim warning about what a can's contents could do to Geraldine's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace or touch of colour or quality.

clue.text: Most enduringly silly minion

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are muddled up
most of a word means all of it except its final letter

explanation.surface: A lackey whose foolishness seems to go on for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: An underling is a subordinate who serves another, as a minion does.

clue.text: Born in Estonia, struggling to be deferential

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are in turmoil

explanation.surface: A person born in Estonia finds it hard to show respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant means showing obeisance, bowing respectfully, so it is a synonym for deferential.

clue.text: About to produce storybooks for customer

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to produce a story is to lie, and books gives NT, the New Testament

explanation.surface: A writer is on the point of bringing out tales for a buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storybooks' splits into 'story' (to produce one is to LIE) and 'books' (NT, the New Testament).
explanation.definitionFit: A client is someone who buys services from a business, a synonym for customer.
